name: Medivh
summary: The Dark Portal stands open, and Medivh's hand has begun the First War. He was the last Guardian of Tirisfal, an ancient order sworn to defend Azeroth from demonic corruption. Yet Sargeras's spirit had bound itself to Medivh before his birth.

sections.title: A Cursed Heritage
sections.body: Born to Aegwynn, a powerful Guardian, and Nielas Aran, a court conjurer, Medivh inherited a cursed legacy. Centuries earlier, Aegwynn fought the fallen Titan Sargeras in Northrend, unaware that his dark essence had slipped into her body to await an heir. On Medivh's fourteenth birthday, the vast magic he inherited from his mother burst forth in a terrifying display. The boy fell into a coma that lasted a decade, watched over by clerics at Northshire Abbey.

sections.title: The Fall of Karazhan
sections.body:
When Medivh awoke, he took up residence in the remote tower of Karazhan. He served as court magus to his childhood friend, King Llane Wrynn of Stormwind. The dark spirit within him slowly wore away his sanity. Seeking to unleash devastation, Medivh reached across the stars to Gul'dan, an orc warlock, and the Shadow Council.

Together they wielded tremendous magic to tear open the Dark Portal. The Horde poured into the Eastern Kingdoms, beginning the First War. Medivh died in his tower at the hands of his closest friend, Anduin Lothar, and his apprentice, Khadgar.

sections.title: The Prophet's Redemption
sections.body:
Medivh returned from beyond death, free of Sargeras and seeking to atone for his crimes. During the Third War, he wore a raven cloak and the guise of an enigmatic Prophet. He warned King Terenas Menethil and Warchief Thrall that the Burning Legion was returning.

Lordaeron ignored his pleas, but Medivh guided Thrall's Horde and Jaina Proudmoore's refugees across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. There, orcs, humans, and night elves united for the decisive stand at Mount Hyjal. Medivh then faded into myth.

faq.answer: Medivh was the last human Guardian of Tirisfal, gifted with immense arcane power to defend Azeroth. Magna Aegwynn was his mother, and he opened the Dark Portal.

faq.q: Why did Medivh open the Dark Portal?
faq.answer: Sargeras's spirit possessed Medivh before he was born. Under its influence, Medivh bargained with the warlock Gul'dan, trading the location of the Tomb of Sargeras for the Horde's invasion of Azeroth and the ruin of the mortal kingdoms.

During the First War, Medivh faced his close friend Anduin Lothar, his apprentice Khadgar, and the half-orc assassin Garona in Karazhan. Khadgar pierced Medivh's heart, and Lothar severed his head, ending his life and casting Sargeras's spirit back into the Nether.

faq.q: What was Medivh's relationship with Stormwind's royalty?
faq.answer: Medivh grew up at Stormwind's royal court alongside Prince Llane Wrynn and Anduin Lothar. The three fought Gurubashi trolls together in their youth, and King Llane trusted Medivh completely. Medivh's betrayal brought devastating grief to the kingdom.
After guiding the mortal races to victory over Archimonde at the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Medivh left for the legends of the past. His whereabouts since are unknown.

Karazhan is a spire atop a potent meeting of ley lines in Deadwind Pass. Aegwynn established the tower, and Medivh later inherited it. Arcane and demonic energies warped it after the Guardian fell, and it remains a haunted ruin.

angles.text: As a Mage, you can see Medivh as both the height of arcane mastery and its peril. Kirin Tor scholars study his fall as a warning against unchecked power.
As a Warlock, you know Medivh's communion with Gul'dan and his place as Sargeras's mortal conduit. His story remains a legendary display of fel summoning and interplanar manipulation.
As an Alliance member, you may remember Medivh with bitter sorrow. Stormwind loved him as a companion to the royal family, yet he brought the ruinous Horde into its lands.
As a member of the Horde, you know Medivh as the human sorcerer whose bargain with Gul'dan opened the Dark Portal and first brought the orcs into this world.
